name: Shell pink
lede: Shell pink is a pale yellowish pink that Werner's 1821 color guide compared to a peach blossom, and it shares its exact hex with another library name, Pale Greyish Vinaceous.

sections.title: Peach blossom and red cobalt ore
sections.body:
Werner's 1821 *Nomenclature of Colours* compares this shade to the vegetable *Peach Blossom* and the mineral *Red Cobalt Ore* [1]. Ridgway's 1912 plates give it at hue 11′′, tone f, on plate XXVIII, and the Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census files it, in block 26, as a pale yellowish pink, Munsell 3.8YR 8.1/2.2 [1]. Maerz and Paul trace the name itself to 1865 [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[iris-mauve]] and [[sandust]], at Its catalogued near-duplicate, *Peach Blossom Red*, comes from Werner directly, within about 1.2 units [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Shell pink in 697 of 23,781 paintings, about 2.9 percent, almost always as a highlight [2]. It peaks in the 1910s, twice its average rate, and concentrates in Xugu's hand, 8 of his 16 dated works, and Niels Skovgaard's, 4 of 14 [2]. Nepalese and Indian paintings carry it far above the archive's base rate [2]. It shares canvases with [[peach]], [[baby-pink]], and [[ecru]] far more than chance alone predicts [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
